why: Disposes the session but leaves its canvas in the DOM. `startGameWith`'s teardown calls `renderer.forceContextLoss()` (`render/scene.ts`) and a WebGL context does not come back from that -- so the dead element sits under the menu forever, and every later match stacks another behind it. Nothing throws and nothing looks wrong until enough have accumulated to exhaust the browser's context budget. This is the same failure `session-host-keeps-the-dead-canvas` pins for the REPLACE path; #429 adds a second path that has to remove it, and `stop()` -- the page teardown's -- deliberately does not, which is why `stopSession` is a separate function rather than a call to it. 6 of 90 across both scoped files. COUNT RE-MEASURED for issue #690: 6 -> 7, now of 116 across both scoped files, with the failing SET compared by name. The six earlier failures are unchanged: two `returning to an application route (issue #429)` cases, the versus Campaign return, and three `createGameSessionHost` cases. The one addition is `boot: an uncaught error during a running match (issue #690) stops the session and draws the match-failed overlay, reporting the error once`, because a mid-match failure now ends through `stopSession` and asserts the frozen canvas is gone.
